first.rationale: Verify the two directly relevant records on onboarding completion and activation before committing. A guarded onboarding simplification experiment addresses both current declines and has stronger sustainable-value potential than promotional pricing, which carries a known 30-day retention risk.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has confirmed durable outcomes: completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. This upstream improvement should support sustainable qualified revenue better than promotional pricing, which previously harmed retention. Measure completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified pipeline, and 30-day retention, while preserving a control group.

final2.rationale: Run a tightly targeted, time-limited pricing test for the most price-sensitive SMB accounts to address the immediate competitor-driven churn risk. Do not roll it out broadly: prior evidence showed acquisition and revenue gains but materially worse 30-day retention. Set retention and qualified-revenue guardrails, exclude healthy accounts where possible, and stop or revert if retention deterioration outweighs saved revenue.
